In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a simple screening test for prolactin secretion which may be used to identify patients with hypothalatic-pituitary dysfunction.
the development of a rapid, reliable method for evaluating the hypothalamic-pituaitary axis.
the study of the regulation of prolactin and the development of new diagnostic tests to evaluate hypothalamic-pitiutary disorders in humans.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
prolactin secretion was normal in 11/23 patients with pituitary disorders, abnormal in 9/23, and undetermined in 3/23 patients.
the prolactin response to TRH is abnormal in patients with hypothalamo-pituitary diseases, but that the response to L-DOPA and CPZ is abnormal only in patients with hypothalmic-pituitary involvement.
the L-Dopa test is a useful and reliable screening test for the diagnosis of hyperprolactinemia.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

(1) L-Dopa is the best test for screening for pituitary disease; (2) TRH is a good test for screening for hypothalamic disease; (3) CPZ is a good test to distinguish between pituitary and hypothalamic disease.
the L-Dopa suppression test is the most sensitive test for the detection of hypothalamic-pitiuitary dysfunction and is particularly helpful in the diagnosis of prolactin-secreting tumors.
prolactin secretion was abnormal in all patients with hypothalomic involvement.
The main takeaway from our work is that

prolactin secretion may be evaluated in patients with suspected hypothalamic-pitiutary disease using the L-Dopa suppression test, chlorpromazine stimulation, and thyrotropine-releasing hormone stimulation.
these three tests have considerable potential for evaluating patients who have suspected pituitary disease.
these tests are a useful way of screening for hypothalamic-pithuitary disease, and that they are a sensitive and specific method for detecting abnormalities in prolactin regulation.
